title: Fire-rated partition at head of wall

checklist.item: The partition's rating and its tested design number are stated.
checklist.why: Layers, stud size and spacing all come from the tested design.

checklist.item: The head-of-wall joint is a tested fire-rated joint system with the same rating, and its number is called out.
checklist.why: The top joint is the usual gap in a rated wall.

checklist.item: A deflection track or slip joint allows the structure above to move, with the movement dimension shown.
checklist.why: A rigid head cracks the wall and breaks the seal.

checklist.item: At fluted deck, the flutes are filled as the joint system requires.
checklist.why: Open flutes are a path over the wall.

checklist.item: Acoustic sealant and the wall's STC rating are shown where the wall is a sound separation.
checklist.why: A sound-rated wall with an open head performs like no wall.

checklist.item: Board layers stop short of the deck by the gap shown, and fasteners are kept out of the slip zone.
checklist.why: Screws through the slip track defeat it.
